rules.title: Integer widening sign- vs zero-extends by source signedness
rules.statement: Widening an integer value to a wider integer type sign-extends when the source type is signed and zero-extends when the source type is unsigned. Unsigned source kinds = {u8,u16,u24,u32,u56,u64,u128} (and bool). bool (i1) is always zero-extended.

rules.title: Integer narrowing truncates
rules.statement: Converting an integer value to a narrower integer type truncates to the destination width (low-order bits retained).

rules.title: Float-to-float widening extends, narrowing truncates
rules.statement: Converting a float to a wider float type extends; to a narrower float type truncates.

rules.title: Integer-to-float conversion respects source signedness
rules.statement: An integer-to-float conversion uses unsigned-to-float when the source integer type is unsigned (one of {u8,u16,u32,u56,u64,u128}), otherwise signed-to-float. Float-to-int is not an implicit coercion and requires an explicit cast.

rules.title: Slice/str values are a 16-byte {data,len} fat pair
rules.statement: A slice type (and str = Slice<u8>) has a fat-pointer representation: a 16-byte {data_ptr, len} pair. Functions returning a slice return this pair by value.

rules.title: Trait-object references are a 16-byte {data,vtable} fat pair
rules.statement: A bare dyn / &dyn / &mut dyn trait object has a 16-byte {data_ptr, vtable_ptr} fat-pointer representation and is returned by value as that pair. A reference to such a reference (Ref/MutRef<TraitObject>) or a raw *const/*mut dyn remains a thin 8-byte pointer.

rules.title: Closure values are a 16-byte {fn,env} fat pair
rules.statement: A closure has a 16-byte {fn_ptr, env_ptr} fat-pointer representation.

rules.title: Custom-DST references are a 16-byte {data,meta} fat pair
rules.statement: A reference to a custom DST (DstRef) has a 16-byte {data_ptr, meta} fat-pointer representation, except a #[self_describing] DST whose metadata is recovered in-band from the header pointer, which is carried as a thin pointer.

rules.title: Plain references and fn pointers are thin 8-byte pointers
rules.statement: A *T, &T, &mut T, or function pointer to a Sized pointee has a thin 8-byte pointer representation.

rules.title: &mut T to a zone_mut type carries its allocator as a fat reference
rules.statement: A &mut T where T is a #[zone_mut] type has a 16-byte {data, zone=*mut Allocator} fat representation, returned by value; the allocator rides the &mut so grow-style methods reach it from &mut self.
rules.divergence: Logos addition: zone/allocator-carrying mutable reference, no Rust analogue.

rules.title: Self-relative (writ / rel_ptr) pointers store a byte offset
rules.statement: A self-relative pointer (the writ / #[rel_ptr] zoned pointer) is stored as an i64 byte offset from the slot's own address; its compute/absolute form is slot_address + load_i64(slot), and lowering stores (target_address - slot_address). A thin-pointer field inside a #[zoned2] struct stores self-relative.
rules.divergence: Logos addition: self-relative zoned pointers, no Rust analogue.

rules.title: Fat-typed aggregate members are stored as an 8-byte pointer
rules.statement: As a struct field, tuple element, or enum payload field: Slice/Closure/Tuple members are stored as an 8-byte pointer (not their by-value fat footprint); struct/enum/array/bare-dyn members are stored inline; an AnyVal member is stored as i32.

rules.title: C-style enum discriminant uses its declared backing type, else i32
rules.statement: A C-style enum's discriminant is represented with its explicitly declared backing integer type (e.g. `enum Foo : u64 {}`); absent an explicit backing type the discriminant defaults to i32.

rules.title: Struct/enum return values are returned by value as the full aggregate
rules.statement: A function returning a Struct/ZonedStruct/Enum returns the literal aggregate value by value (the registered LLVM struct/tagged-enum type), even though such types are passed by pointer at parameter/field/scope positions.

rules.title: Struct types are identified by package-qualified name
rules.statement: A struct type's identity carries its package prefix (pkg.Name); same-named structs in different packages are distinct types and do not alias. Method-symbol mangling uses the package-agnostic bare struct name.

rules.title: Owned closures drop their owned captures then free an escaping env
rules.statement: Dropping an owned closure value runs per-closure drop glue that drops each owned droppable capture (the narrow captured field when RFC-2229 phase-2 narrowing applies, else the whole captured root) and, if the env is heap-allocated (escaping closure), frees the env.
